newsitem.title: USA: Orion Network Systems to top junk issuance.
newsitem.headline: Orion Network Systems to top junk issuance.

text.p: The high-yield new issue docket for Tuesday is expected to be topped by a $710 million two-tranche issue from Orion Network Systems, dealers said.

Orion, an international satellite communications company, more than doubled increased the size of the offering on Monday reflecting the powerful demand created by the extremely tight yield spreads in taxable fixed-income product, a dealer said.

With the proceeds, Orion is expected to "fully realize its business plan," which includes a major expansion of its services into the Asia Pacific region with a second satellite, according to a source close to the deal.
A third Orion Satellite is expected to be announced soon.

The B2/single-B rated deal will be formally priced by late afternoon on Tuesday by a Morgan Stanley & Co syndicate. Street talk suggested the issue will include $445 million senior 10-year debt priced with a coupon at or near 11-1/4 percent and $265 million discount notes at an additional 125 to 150 basis points.
The issue is also expected to carry warrants.

Already priced on Tuesday were $200 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via a Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp syndicate. The B2/single-B rated notes were priced in the 144a market at par to yield 10 percent.
Other issues set to come include:
--$150 million 144A cumulative exchangeable pay-in-kind (PIK) preferred stock from Granite Broadcasting Corp via a Goldman Sachs & Co group. The deal will have a 2009 maturity.

Separately, high-yield issuance continued to trade at a premium to issued prices. Tenet HealthCare Corp's $400 million senior notes due 2003 were quoted at 100-1/8 compared with the issued price of 99.924; $900 million senior notes due 2005 were quoted at 99.75 bid compared with the issued price of 99.358; and $700 million senior subordinated noted due 2007 were quoted at 100-7/8 to 101-3/8 compared with the issued price of 99.894.

Investment grade debt, meanwhile, was led by a $300 million 30put10 issue from Korea Electric Power Corp. The A1/AA-minus rated debentures were priced on Tuesday at par with a seven percent coupon for a yield spread of 45 basis points over Treasuries.
Trust preferreds from Union Carbide and TIG Capital Trust may price as early as Tuesday, syndicates said.
